title: Projective Hodge lines and ordinary Iitaka subadditivity
main_claim: Iitaka's conjecture C_{n,m}: for f:X->Z an algebraic fibre space of smooth projective varieties over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, kappa(X) >= kappa(F) + kappa(Z). The key input is Thm 1.2 ("projective adjoint positivity"). It says that a nef Q-divisor M realized by the whole highest Hodge line of a rational VHS satisfies M ~_Q p^*L for a fibre space p:Y->S, with K_S + jL big for j >> 0.

issues.description: The numerical-rank identity nu(J) = rank of d(ell) rests on the claim that the extended top Hodge line is big exactly when the top Kodaira-Spencer map is generically injective. This is attributed to BBT Lemma 6.17 and I could not check that the cited lemma says exactly this. The statement is standard-looking: Mumford-good metric, curvature kernel equal to ker(theta). Still, the 'only if' direction, which is needed so that J|_{C_a} is not big when a > r, depends on the boundary contributing nothing to J^a. That holds only if the cited result really covers it.
issues.evidence: "It is big precisely when the top Kodaira--Spencer map ... is generically injective ... The second assertion is \cite[Lemma~6.17]{BakkerBrunebarbeTsimerman}."

issues.description: Brunebarbe-Cadorel Thm 1.1 is applied to the extended pure variation on U_N = T \ D_N to get K_T + D_N big. Its hypotheses (quasi-unipotent or discrete monodromy, immersive at one point) are not restated. They appear to hold here (neat Gamma', unipotent monodromy, T birational to the period image), so this looks like a citation-precision point, not a gap.
issues.evidence: "The log-general-type theorem for a polarized variation with generically immersive period map therefore gives K_T+D_N big. Here the applicable theorem is \cite[Theorem~1.1]{BrunebarbeCadorel}."

coverage:
I read all of the main route, Secs 1-7 (main.tex and sections 01-07), line by line.
- Sec 2: checked the minimal-subvariation construction, the normal-subgroup lemma (André normality plus the P-stability argument) and the flat-automorphism lemma (commutator normal closure, centralizing G, fixed-part theorem on the finite étale cover).
- Sec 3: checked the numerical-rank proposition via general complete intersections. Checked the boundary-line proposition (Deligne bigrading, primitivity of the top line, the N^l projection bound) and the tangential rank principle proof (contraction / constant-rank argument). Verified the expansion in the nilpotent-limit lemma by hand.
- Sec 4: checked the rank-loss theorem in both cases. Nilpotent case: G_N is generated by conjugates of exp(tN), so Lemma 2.2 kills it. Finite-inertia case: eigenline argument, then Lemma 2.3, then phi(by)=phi(y), then birationality T~B. Also checked r>0.
- Sec 5: checked the volume lemma. The section-count bound difference identity, the O(j^{r-1}) estimate and the c j^r lower bound all verify. Also checked the exceptional-pullback lemma, descent of J'^{|H|} through the kernel of H->G_f, the class identity M ~ p_0^*L_0 via injectivity of generically finite pullback, the Jacobian split R_div/R_exc with inertia fixing ramified divisors pointwise, and the Stein factorization step.
- Sec 6: checked the least-index normalization, the all-degree direct-image argument, discriminant coefficients in [0,1) (t_P>0), the root-cover lemma (Kummer irreducibility, K_W <= h^*(K_C+D_C)+E, kappa=0, p_g=1) and both section comparisons.
- Sec 7: checked the period-fibre nonvanishing lemma (the cotangent-filtration morphism h_s^*omega_Z -> omega_{W_s} and the KP application on r_s) and the weak-positivity effectivity lemma (twist arithmetic beta/(k l)=1/(k alpha), pushforward of poles). Checked the interpolation identity lambda*E_1 + (1-lambda)*E_2 = K+B+M with lambda j + (1-lambda) v = 1, the final KP/Hashizume application, and scalar extension.
- Not audited: Secs 8-9. They are alternative proofs of the boundary estimate and are not used by the main route; no label from 08/09 is referenced in 02-07.
- Not verified: the content of cited deep theorems (FM Thm 4.5, Ambro, BBT, BC, KP/Hashizume, Fujino weak positivity) beyond whether their stated hypotheses are plausibly met.
